Witty

/WIT-ee/ — rhymes with pretty · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Witty describes someone who is clever and quick at making amusing remarks.

Her witty acceptance speech had the audience laughing within seconds.

Worked Example

During the quiz bowl, the team's best player cracked jokes so cleverly timed and unexpectedly funny that judges actually paused to laugh.

This captures more than just being funny—it's being quick, clever, and making amusing remarks all at once. The sharpness and speed of the quips matter as much as the humor. 'Funny' wouldn't capture this precision; witty does.

How Witty Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

clever

clever: quick and intelligent in thinking

humorous

humorous: funny; causing laughter or amusement

sharp-witted

sharp-witted: mentally quick, fast with comebacks

Antonyms

dull

dull: boring, with no spark or humor

humorless

humorless: unable to make or enjoy jokes

How Strong Is It? — amusing → clever → funny → witty

amusing vs. witty

amusing vs. witty: Amusing covers anything mildly entertaining, but witty requires real cleverness and speed behind the humor.

clever vs. witty

clever vs. witty: Clever means intelligent in general, while witty focuses that intelligence into quick, funny remarks.

funny vs. witty

funny vs. witty: Funny describes anything that makes you laugh; witty is stronger because the laughs come from sharp, rapid cleverness.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — wit

Root — wit: quick intelligence, understanding (Old English (witt))

Suffix — -y

Suffix — -y: full of, characterized by (Old English (-ig))

Put it together

Put it together: Wit is an old word for quick intelligence, and -y means 'full of' — so witty literally means 'full of wit': bursting with quick, clever humor.

Use the root in a new word: outwit

Use the root in a new word: outwit: The clever rabbit doubled back on its own tracks to outwit the fox.

Word Choice

neutral

Witty is lighter and faster than 'clever'—it's about quick, amusing remarks rather than deep thinking. Reach for witty when the cleverness shines through jokes or quick comebacks, not just smart problem-solving.
